map_spec.title: The Lantern Marches
map_spec.purpose: Player-facing exploration atlas for choosing routes between a fortified city, wild country and uncanny landmarks. Not a token-scale battlemap.

inspiration.premise: A river kingdom survives under an ancient astronomical citadel, while three glass monoliths awaken on its eastern frontier.

references.source: Visual observations from the user-provided regional-map screenshot; image bytes are not bundled.
use_traits: pictorial mountains and buildings within overhead geography
ignore_traits: original place names and exact geography

style.medium: Fine ink-and-watercolor fantasy cartography with carefully drawn miniature architecture.
style.linework: Thin charcoal contours; finer hatching inside landforms; distinct silhouettes without heavy comic outlines.
style.surface_texture: Subtle matte paper tooth, not distressed parchment stains. Low-contrast texture in open land and water.
style.lighting: Soft overcast daylight with light coming from upper left; gentle relief shading, no cast shadows hiding paths.

environment.terrain_summary: A broad south-draining valley between a wooded western slope and a steep eastern plateau. Northern mountains frame the citadel; the southern river mouth opens to the sea.
exceptions: The three glass spires are supernatural constructions; their shapes need not follow natural geology. Rivers and travel routes otherwise follow plausible terrain.

citadel.name: Crown of Tides
citadel.appearance: A compact limestone city on a low escarpment, encircled by terraced walls and crowned by a single enormous tilted bronze astronomical ring. The ring is the unique regional silhouette.
must_show: one oversized bronze ring, not a skull

western_wood.name: The Pale Boughs
western_wood.appearance: A dense wedge of white-barked forest with a few leaning old trunks and small clearings, drawn as coherent wooded masses rather than evenly scattered tree icons.
western_wood.gameplay_role: A slower wilderness route on the west side of the valley

northern_ridge.name: The Rimeback
northern_ridge.appearance: An irregular chain of pale angular peaks, taller to the northeast, lower at the central pass.

glass_spires.name: The Three Listeners
glass_spires.appearance: Exactly three tall, narrow smoky-glass monoliths rise from a flat basalt shelf. One is visibly tilted, one split at its top, and one intact. Space them so they remain individually countable.
must_show: a visible ascending trail from the west
glass_spires.gameplay_role: Eastern exploration objective visible from far away

copper_marsh.name: The Ember Reeds
copper_marsh.appearance: A low copper-and-rust reed marsh with dark pools and a few raised hummocks, providing the sole warm color mass in the lower-right region.
copper_marsh.gameplay_role: A hazardous optional detour, not a wall of vegetation

river.name: The Lowwater
river.appearance: A connected slate-blue river descending from below the citadel through the valley and into a small southern delta. Keep upstream narrower and downstream broader.
river.gameplay_role: Divides travel choices and establishes the valley direction

stone_bridge.name: The Last Arch
stone_bridge.appearance: A single worn pale-stone arch spanning the narrow river, with visibly connected approaches on both banks.
must_show: the river remains visible below the arch

south_port.name: Lantern Quay
south_port.appearance: A small fishing and caravan port on the western river mouth, with clustered low roofs, two short jetties and a warm beacon tower.

watchtower.name: The Leaning Watch
watchtower.appearance: One roofless square watchtower leaning slightly on a low grassy knoll. The missing upper corner makes it recognizable at small scale.

south_sea.name: The Somber Reach
south_sea.appearance: A calm strip of blue-gray coastal water at the lower edge; the Lowwater visibly empties here.

sealed_observatory.name: The Sealed Observatory
sealed_observatory.appearance: A small concealed observatory chamber within the citadel.
sealed_observatory.gm_notes: The green dial unlocks the room at midnight. Do not include the chamber, its marker or this fact in a player-facing image.

pilgrim_road.appearance: A pale packed-earth road, clearly differentiated from the blue river; it crosses only at the stone bridge.

spire_ascent.appearance: A narrow switchback ascent with a believable ramp onto the basalt shelf.

western_branch.appearance: A secondary dirt trail across open grass with occasional broken boundary stones.

marsh_detour.appearance: A narrow raised path ending at the marsh edge; do not conceal its entrance.

relationships.detail: The city sits upstream above the river crossing.
The spires occupy the eastern plateau, not the western forest.
Keep the watchtower on the same western side as the port approach.
The arch crosses the actual river, not a neighboring dry channel.
The river outlet meets the coastal water without a strip of land blocking it.
This relationship is private and absent from player art.

affordances: a fast main road versus optional rough detours
a high eastern landmark visible from lower terrain
must_preserve: distinct silhouettes for city, spires and watchtower
broad quiet areas for reading terrain

annotations.typography: Small-cap serif geographic labels, dark charcoal, restrained tracking; add outside the image generator.

clear_zones.purpose: low-detail ground for the citadel label

must_include: a readable network of public travel routes
must_avoid: borrowed place names from the reference
production.revision_notes: Original demonstration setting. The supplied screenshot informed broad visual traits, not copied names or geography.

compiled.image_instructions:
DELIVERABLE
One regional map for tabletop play, 16:9 composition. Overhead geographic composition with pictorial oblique mountains and buildings; no horizon or cinematic landscape camera.
Purpose: Player-facing exploration atlas for choosing routes between a fortified city, wild country and uncanny landmarks. Not a token-scale battlemap.
Working title (not automatically printed): The Lantern Marches.

INTENT AND COMPOSITION
Premise: A river kingdom survives under an ancient astronomical citadel, while three glass monoliths awaken on its eastern frontier.
Mood: wonder, weathered grandeur, inviting mystery. Novelty: balanced.
Motifs: bronze astronomical circles; pale limestone; amber reeds
A broad south-draining valley between a wooded western slope and a steep eastern plateau. Northern mountains frame the citadel; the southern river mouth opens to the sea.
Primary visual anchor: Crown of Tides. Read in this order: Crown of Tides > The Three Listeners > The Lowwater > The Ember Reeds > Lantern Quay.
Keep critical content inside an edge safety inset of 3.0%. North is up. Coordinates below use image space: x left-to-right, y top-to-bottom; every percentage is relative to the complete canvas. These are layout instructions, not drawn coordinate labels.

VISUAL LANGUAGE
Fine ink-and-watercolor fantasy cartography with carefully drawn miniature architecture.
Linework: Thin charcoal contours; finer hatching inside landforms; distinct silhouettes without heavy comic outlines.
Palette by role: accent: #B77543; forest: #899779; paper: #E5E0D3; stone: #B5B5A8; water: #728B9A
Surface: Subtle matte paper tooth, not distressed parchment stains. Low-contrast texture in open land and water.
Lighting: Soft overcast daylight with light coming from upper left; gentle relief shading, no cast shadows hiding paths.
Detail density: dense. Border: none; edge-to-edge geographic artwork. Concentrate small detail around important places; protect terrain silhouettes and readable routes.

ENVIRONMENT
Season: early autumn. Time: late morning. Weather: clear air under thin cloud. Physical logic: mythic. Explicit exceptions: The three glass spires are supernatural constructions; their shapes need not follow natural geology. Rivers and travel routes otherwise follow plausible terrain.

REQUIRED MAP CONTENT
citadel | Crown of Tides | fort | primary | quantity 1. box left 43.0%, top 16.0%, width 22.0%, height 20.0%. A compact limestone city on a low escarpment, encircled by terraced walls and crowned by a single enormous tilted bronze astronomical ring. The ring is the unique regional silhouette.
Must show: one oversized bronze ring, not a skull; three stepped wall terraces; one clear south-facing approach.
Do not show here: a second ring; a floating city; a skull-shaped tower.
Spatial function: Main destination and navigational anchor.

glass_spires | The Three Listeners | landmark | primary | quantity 3. box left 75.0%, top 30.0%, width 19.0%, height 34.0%. Exactly three tall, narrow smoky-glass monoliths rise from a flat basalt shelf. One is visibly tilted, one split at its top, and one intact. Space them so they remain individually countable.
Must show: exactly three separate monoliths; three different silhouettes; a visible ascending trail from the west.
Do not show here: extra miniature spires; floating rocks.
Spatial function: Eastern exploration objective visible from far away.

copper_marsh | The Ember Reeds | terrain | supporting | quantity 1. box left 59.0%, top 70.0%, width 21.0%, height 17.0%. A low copper-and-rust reed marsh with dark pools and a few raised hummocks, providing the sole warm color mass in the lower-right region.
Must show: water visible between reed masses.
Spatial function: A hazardous optional detour, not a wall of vegetation.

river | The Lowwater | river | supporting | quantity 1. box left 32.0%, top 32.0%, width 25.0%, height 64.0%. A connected slate-blue river descending from below the citadel through the valley and into a small southern delta. Keep upstream narrower and downstream broader.
Shape path: (54.0% across, 34.0% down) -> (55.0% across, 41.0% down) -> (52.0% across, 48.0% down) -> (51.0% across, 55.0% down) -> (49.0% across, 64.0% down) -> (44.0% across, 74.0% down) -> (37.0% across, 85.0% down) -> (34.0% across, 95.0% down).
Must show: one continuous connected watercourse; a visible southern outlet.
Do not show here: water flowing uphill; random disconnected river fragments.
Spatial function: Divides travel choices and establishes the valley direction.

south_port | Lantern Quay | settlement | supporting | quantity 1. box left 25.0%, top 83.0%, width 15.0%, height 11.0%. A small fishing and caravan port on the western river mouth, with clustered low roofs, two short jetties and a warm beacon tower.
Must show: two short jetties; one small beacon tower.
Spatial function: Southern campaign entry point.

stone_bridge | The Last Arch | bridge | supporting | quantity 1. box left 46.5%, top 52.5%, width 10.0%, height 6.0%. A single worn pale-stone arch spanning the narrow river, with visibly connected approaches on both banks.
Must show: both bridge ends meet land; the river remains visible below the arch.
Spatial function: A strategically legible chokepoint.

watchtower | The Leaning Watch | landmark | supporting | quantity 1. box left 18.0%, top 64.0%, width 5.5%, height 9.0%. One roofless square watchtower leaning slightly on a low grassy knoll. The missing upper corner makes it recognizable at small scale.
Must show: one missing upper corner.
Spatial function: Western exploration objective.

northern_ridge | The Rimeback | mountain | ambient | quantity 1. box left 33.0%, top 3.5%, width 60.0%, height 12.0%. An irregular chain of pale angular peaks, taller to the northeast, lower at the central pass.
Must show: a visible central pass.
Spatial function: Northern geographic boundary.

south_sea | The Somber Reach | water | ambient | quantity 1. box left 2.0%, top 93.5%, width 96.0%, height 6.5%. A calm strip of blue-gray coastal water at the lower edge; the Lowwater visibly empties here.
Spatial function: Southern boundary and river outlet.

western_wood | The Pale Boughs | forest | ambient | quantity 1. box left 6.0%, top 24.0%, width 27.0%, height 37.0%. A dense wedge of white-barked forest with a few leaning old trunks and small clearings, drawn as coherent wooded masses rather than evenly scattered tree icons.
Must show: two or three broad clearings.
Spatial function: A slower wilderness route on the west side of the valley.

ROUTES AND ACCESS
marsh_detour: trail; The Last Arch -> The Ember Reeds. Traversable. Route shape: (51.0% across, 55.0% down) -> (57.0% across, 62.0% down) -> (62.0% across, 68.0% down) -> (67.0% across, 77.0% down). A narrow raised path ending at the marsh edge; do not conceal its entrance.
pilgrim_road: road; Lantern Quay -> The Last Arch -> Crown of Tides. Traversable. Route shape: (32.5% across, 88.5% down) -> (36.0% across, 78.0% down) -> (43.0% across, 66.0% down) -> (51.0% across, 55.0% down) -> (58.0% across, 44.0% down) -> (54.0% across, 29.0% down). A pale packed-earth road, clearly differentiated from the blue river; it crosses only at the stone bridge.
spire_ascent: trail; Crown of Tides -> The Three Listeners. Traversable. Route shape: (54.0% across, 29.0% down) -> (65.0% across, 34.0% down) -> (72.0% across, 43.0% down) -> (82.0% across, 46.0% down). A narrow switchback ascent with a believable ramp onto the basalt shelf.
western_branch: trail; The Last Arch -> The Leaning Watch. Traversable. Route shape: (51.0% across, 55.0% down) -> (39.0% across, 60.0% down) -> (30.0% across, 63.0% down) -> (20.5% across, 68.5% down). A secondary dirt trail across open grass with occasional broken boundary stones.

SPATIAL RELATIONSHIPS
MUST: Crown of Tides north of The Last Arch. The city sits upstream above the river crossing.
MUST: The Three Listeners east of The Lowwater. The spires occupy the eastern plateau, not the western forest.
MUST: The Leaning Watch west of The Lowwater. Keep the watchtower on the same western side as the port approach.
MUST: The Last Arch crosses The Lowwater. The arch crosses the actual river, not a neighboring dry channel.
MUST: The Lowwater flows into The Somber Reach. The river outlet meets the coastal water without a strip of land blocking it.

PLAYABILITY
Affordances: a river chokepoint; a fast main road versus optional rough detours; a high eastern landmark visible from lower terrain
Preserve: the public route graph; distinct silhouettes for city, spires and watchtower; an unbroken river outlet; broad quiet areas for reading terrain
Keep the declared traversable routes visibly continuous between entry points and objectives; do not seal openings with props or decoration.

GRID, TEXT AND UI
Do not paint a square grid, hex grid, coordinate numbers or grid intersections. Grid setup is handled separately.
Do not paint any titles, names, text, numbers or legends. Location names in these instructions identify objects only; lettering is a separate layer.
Do not draw VTT pins, tokens, mouse pointers, toolbars or interface chrome. Keep these regions visually quiet for overlays, without drawing blank boxes: box left 43.0%, top 36.5%, width 22.0%, height 3.5%: low-detail ground for the citadel label

REFERENCE DIRECTION
Reference regional-reference, role style: use fine hand-inked terrain; restrained watercolor washes; pictorial mountains and buildings within overhead geography; one dominant architectural landmark; varied regional silhouettes. Ignore original place names and exact geography; numbered hex overlay; mouse pointer; interface pins; cropped banner.
Use references only for their assigned roles; create the specified new geography unless a layout reference explicitly requires otherwise.

FINAL PRIORITIES
Required objects, their quantities, spatial relationships and readable routes take precedence over decorative density. Do not replace a difficult required feature with a generic substitute.
Must include: a uniquely recognizable astronomical citadel; three countable glass spires; a readable network of public travel routes
Avoid: borrowed place names from the reference; UI screenshots; cursor arrows; painted VTT markers; photorealistic satellite terrain; a cinematic horizon; unrequested text; standing character tokens

setup_steps: Produce and inspect a player-safe base image; keep the editable master specification private.
Open Atlas VTT: Open dashboard in desktop Obsidian; choose the intended collection.
Import the local image with the asset manager + button, then create a scene from the map asset.
Align the grid manually; auto detection is an option for an image with an existing grid, not proof of correct alignment.
Add labels with Atlas text tools or a separately prepared overlay. Link Markdown or Atlas maps with note pins; pins are GM preparation aids.
Place tokens and configure fog, walls and lighting separately in Atlas as needed.
Present the scene in the separate player window, inspect disclosure, then reopen the scene to verify persistence.
calibration_notes: All settings are candidates for manual calibration against the actual imported image.
Atlas has no mi unitType; converted distance to feet. Confirm the displayed scale.
acceptance_checks: Inspect actual image dimensions and compare several cell spacings across the image after alignment.
Test token snapping and a known movement distance, including hex orientation if applicable.
Inspect the player window for unintended labels, tokens, secrets and revealed areas. Baked image content cannot be removed by GM visibility flags.
Reopen the .atlasmap scene and confirm background, grid and authored objects persist.
